novelty_flags.label: prop:published-tree-boundary
novelty_flags.one_line: This node expressly restates Gupta--Bläser Theorem 27, so it is published prior art rather than a novel to-prove result and should be moved to contextual boundary material.

soundness_flags.label: def:regular-class; thm:regular-finite-set-inference
soundness_flags.one_line: Finite complex degree does not ensure that the retained real set is nonempty, yet d_H is defined only for nonempty finite sets and the root labels and simultaneous ellipsoid require J>=1.

soundness_flags.label: ass:denominator-margin; ass:simple-roots
soundness_flags.one_line: On a compact class contained in M_G minus E_G,e, the nonzero certificate circuits are uniformly bounded away from zero; with the squarefreeness circuit and bounded monic coefficients, the corresponding uniform simple-root margin is derivable rather than an independent class assumption.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:regular-finite-set-inference and prop:singleton-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Accept inference only conditionally on a fixed finite-degree graph-query and a compact smooth regular component away from certificate, discriminant, and real-lift boundaries.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform root-m inference and branchwise Gaussian coverage only on a revised nonempty regular finite-real-fiber component; no claim is made at discriminants or under branch selection.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 27 states Algorithm 2 is correct, and Algorithm 2 decides for each tree coefficient whether it is generically identifiable, 2-identifiable, or unidentifiable.
TreeID uses missing bidirected cycles and quadratic reductions, runs in polynomial space, and the original paper says completeness for tree models was possible but not proved.
The paper improves the complete tree-shaped-SCM algorithm to O(n^3 log^2 n), implements it, and describes Gupta--Bläser's tree algorithm as complete.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 13, Appendix A.3, Theorem 17 and Corollary 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary 6 states that generic edge identifiability can be decided in PSPACE; it does not output a coordinate minimal polynomial.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv corroborating version of the Annals of Statistics article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies finite-to-one examples and exhaustive calculations through five nodes, and its residual equations are the missing-disturbance constraints; this corroboration was not used to allege a primary-source formula mismatch.
The paper returns a rational identifying formula of prespecified maximum degree in quasi-polynomial time when one exists.
The paper treats generic parametrization and specialization of generically zero-dimensional parametric polynomial systems.
The paper derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Move the Gupta--Bläser tree trichotomy out of the root statement list into a cited boundary lemma/context paragraph, and keep the positive-excess frontier as the first novel theorem-level target.

Define the regular inference domain with R_e(G,Sigma) nonempty and either define d_H for empty estimates or prove the estimator is nonempty on an explicit high-probability neighborhood; then derive rather than assume redundant compact-away-from-bad-locus margins.

Make the five-node census the first deliverable and publish its characteristic-zero orbit table, including any orientation-count losses, before asserting the all-size recurrence and FPT eliminant theorem.

Add a sharp comparison theorem against both the Gupta--Bläser tree output and the Dörfler et al. PSPACE edge-decision output, specifying the strict output-domain gain of the proposed certificate on tree-plus-k inputs.

recommended_next_step: Revise the known-tree proposition and nonempty regular inference domain, then advance the repaired field-tier frontier kernel to Stage 0.
